source.title: Talking Heads: Understanding Inter-layer Communication in Transformer Language Models
source.authors: Jack Merullo; Carsten Eickhoff; Ellie Pavlick

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure and appendix content is flattened or garbled in the extraction, but the main text and its relevant descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper mentions the Superposition Hypothesis in related work but does not test sparse-feature superposition. Its experiments concern low-rank communication channels and context indexing, a different mechanism.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about low-rank communication channels and a three-dimensional context-indexing mechanism. These are recorded as related findings, not evidence for or against the listed superposition versions. References to the original superposition work are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The paper finds low-rank (1–3D) communication channels between attention heads via SVD of weight matrices and studies a context-indexing capacity limit. It cites the Superposition Hypothesis only in related work. It does not measure sparse features outnumbering dimensions, neuron polysemanticity, SAE features, or whether superposed features are 1-D. The 'capacity' it reports concerns a 3D positional-index subspace crowded by list items, not feature superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors also stress three further points. Weight-based SVD decomposition can recover known circuit interactions without running the model. Low-rank channels carry content-independent positional signals. The indexing channel's limited capacity helps explain prompt-order sensitivity and failures on longer lists.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes transformer weight matrices with SVD and performs activation and weight interventions; it does not reproduce the original toy-model setup or its sparse-feature/superposition measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The indexing-space structure and task performance vary with the number of objects; the paper reports fragmentation around 9 or 10 objects.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT2-Small, a 3D subspace spanned by three inhibition components partitions by attended object index. The partitions fragment around 9–10 objects. Answer-conditioned interventions in this subspace raise Laundry List accuracy (3 objects: 64%→86%; 8 objects: ~51%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learned low-dimensional context-indexing channel has finite capacity that limits retrieval from longer lists.

fits_no_version.finding: Inhibition and duplicate-token signals between attention heads are carried mainly by one or two SVD components (rank-1/rank-2 channels). Removing the top component cuts the inhibition score by 7–14%. The same pattern appears in Pythia-160m.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inter-layer communication between attention heads uses very low-rank subspaces of the residual stream.

record.problems: The paper focuses heavily on GPT2-Small and uses synthetic tasks. Some reported intervention and geometry results are qualitative or described approximately, and the listed accuracy values have no uncertainty estimates in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Other communication-channel, IOI, and open-domain results were not included because they do not measure the listed superposition versions or add a distinct context-indexing outcome beyond the rows recorded.

untested.parts: No toy model, no sparsity manipulation, no measurement of overlapping nearly orthogonal feature directions or phase transition.
No neuron-level polysemanticity analysis or feature-importance allocation of dimensions.
No test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
No measurement of features spread across neurons and no SAE or dictionary recovery.
Rank-1 inhibition components and a 2D duplicate-token channel are found. Superposition of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly marked versions ['none']. The record's cites_only/T6 classification is right. The paper's 'capacity' and 'crowding' language concerns a positional-index subspace, not superposition of sparse features.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse features competing for dimensions, nearly orthogonal overlapping directions, or a sparsity-dependent transition and geometry.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Does not measure feature distribution across neurons or recover features with an SAE or dictionary.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Finds low-rank communication signals, including rank-1 components, but does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Traversed the three-dimensional space spanned by three inhibition-head components and measured which object the mover head attended to.

conditions.value: varied; structure breaks down around 9 or 10 objects

rows.measure: Organization of the three-dimensional space by attended object index
rows.value: The space partitions into regions for object indices; the regions become small and begin to fracture around 9 or 10 objects.
rows.note: This is a context-indexing channel result, not a measurement of superposed sparse features.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Set the model's inhibition components to a region of the three-dimensional space selected using the correct answer's index.
rows.note: An intervention that uses the indexing channel; it does not establish sparse-feature superposition.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Set the model's inhibition components to a region of the three-dimensional space selected using the correct answer's index.
rows.note: The paper says this is about the level of the unmodified model with 4 objects; it does not state the unmodified 8-object accuracy in the text.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Scaled one inhibition component at a time and measured the mover head's attention in the multi-object task.
rows.measure: Ability to direct the mover head's attention among the candidate objects
rows.value: One component at a time did not provide enough expressive power to direct attention to all objects; the model tended to attend to the first or last object.
rows.note: The text reports this result qualitatively.
